svg.title: Echo and Rouw: a partner's Eigen, the Echo that tracks it, and the Echo that outlives it
svg.desc: One member's Echo of its partner, from the formal structure of the Speelgoed (Sections II, VIII.1 and VIII.6). While the Koppel lives, the partner's Eigen e_j moves and the Echo h_i follows it by the delay filter tau·dh/dt = e_j(t − delta) − h_i + upsilon: it hears every change late, by the Vertraging delta; it closes on it gradually, at the rate set by the Ontspanning tau; and it is never exact, because of the Vervorming upsilon. The distance between the Eigen and the Echo is the Echo gap, a real and queryable quantity. At t0 the Koppel ends. The filter's input freezes at the last transmitted value e_j(t0 − delta); the Echo relaxes toward it and then wanders around it under its own distortion, permanently. That is Rouw: the Echo gap can no longer be measured, and the equation has no decay-to-deletion term. The curves are a simulation of the equation with arbitrary values; they carry no scale.
svg.text: τ · ḣᵢ(t) = eⱼ(t − δ) − hᵢ(t) + υᵢ(t)
τ · ḣᵢ(t) = eⱼ(t₀ − δ) − hᵢ(t) + υᵢ(t)
the input freezes at eⱼ(t₀ − δ),
the last thing it ever received
no live Eigen to compare against:
While the Koppel lives, the Echo hears each change late
(δ), closes on it gradually (τ), and is never a clean
copy (υ). The gap between Eigen and Echo is real and
queryable: how wrong a system is about its partner.
When the Koppel ends, the Echo settles toward the last
signal it received and drifts under its own distortion,
a record more of the mourner than of the departed.
Quiet is not gone: touch it, and it answers.
An Echo always outlives its Koppel. Rouw is permanent:
the equation has no decay-to-deletion term, and none may be added.
The curves simulate the filter with arbitrary values; they carry no scale.
